Caption: 

# From playground to Parliament

Pokémon trading cards were causing trouble on playgrounds around the US almost as soon as they made their debut in January 1999.

In May, the_ LA Times _[reported](https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-may-30-mn-42491-story.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) on measures schools were taking to combat the cards’ disruptive influence: _Kids Told to Pocket Their Pokémons_, the headline read.

“The children are beginning to become obsessed by them,” a principal who had banned trading between pupils said. “Some of our younger kids were getting suckered out of their more valuable cards.”

In other schools, they were banned entirely. A 7-year-old told the _Times_ he didn’t bring his cards to school anymore because “the principal said he’d better not catch us trading.”

With a hint of disbelief, the _Times_ noted that the rarest cards were selling for more than $50 each.

In October, the _Times_ [reported](https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-oct-16-mn-22915-story.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) that the situation had escalated: _Backlash Builds as Schoolyards Evolve Into Pokémon Trading Pits_.

“School officials from Connecticut to California have concluded the cards are disrupting learning, poisoning playground friendships and causing such distraction that some children forget their homework, tune out in class and even miss school buses as they scramble to acquire one more card.”

One principal told the _Times_ that children “were bringing cash wads of up to $40 to school, hoping to buy a coveted card.”

This set Pokémon apart from all previous schoolyard crazes.

“The thing with the Pokémon cards is that kids are really aware of their value,” a child psychologist said. At his son’s school, it had turned recess “into a little flea market,” he added. “They had their calculators out. It really became a buy-and-sell bazaar.”

The Daily ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by Daniel Kuhn | Edited by Kyle Baird

Happy Monday! Daniel here. I'll be covering The Daily for James this week. *Bitcoin* dropped as low as $63,750 this weekend before rebounding above $65,600 early on Monday, and is currently trading around $64,900.

In today's newsletter, *Strategy* sold *MSTR* to bump its *USD reserve* to $3.75 billion, *Ondo* debuted a new execution network that will support *perps* , *Lido* updated its largest Curated Module offering, paving the way to slash the number of *Ethereum* *validators* , and more.

Meanwhile, South Korea's *KB Kookmin Bank* is building a cross-border payment service ( https://www.theblock.co/post/409702/kb-kookmin-bank-payment-jpmorgans-kinexys?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) on *JPMorgan's Kinexys* , according to local reports.

It's a great read — and just like The Daily , it's free to subscribe ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters?select=The%20Funding&utm_campaign=website&utm_campaign=website&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_medium=referral&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=newsletter&utm_source=newsletter&utm_source=newsletter&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) !

*THE BIG ONE*

*💵 Strategy extends bitcoin pause to 5 weeks, sells $544.5 million in MSTR as USD reserve hits $3.75 billion*

CZ ( https://www.theblock.co/post/409721/strategy-extends-bitcoin-pause-to-five-weeks-sells-544-5-million-in-mstr-as-usd-reserve-hits-3-75-billion?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*Strategy* made no bitcoin purchases for a fifth consecutive week as the company announced another *MSTR sale* , this time offering about 5.4 million MSTR shares for $544.5 million.

* The firm's *USD reserve* rose to around $3.75 billion as of July 26, while its bitcoin holdings remain unchanged at 843,775 BTC, worth about $54.7 billion, purchased at an average price of roughly $75,476 per coin.
* This activity extends a recent shift toward building cash reserves and liquidity rather than adding to its bitcoin stack since its last purchase on June 22.
* Strategy launched its so-called *Digital Credit Capital Framework* , requiring it to hold enough liquidity to cover at least 12 months of preferred-stock dividends and debt interest, after *STRC* lost its $1 peg ( https://www.theblock.co/post/405160/strategys-strc-preferred-stock-closes-day-89?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) last month.

**gm, Defiers!**

These were the biggest stories in crypto and DeFi today:

* **[Ether ETFs](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/ether-etfs-pull-104m-tripling-bitcoin-s-weekly-inflows)**[ pull $104M, tripling bitcoin's inflows](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/ether-etfs-pull-104m-tripling-bitcoin-s-weekly-inflows)

* **[Circle](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/circle-buys-ibm-blockchain-patent-portfolio)**[ buys IBM's blockchain patent portfolio](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/circle-buys-ibm-blockchain-patent-portfolio)

* **[Lido](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/lido-unveils-curated-module-v2-in-ethereum-staking-overhaul)**[ overhauls ETH staking with bonded operators](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/lido-unveils-curated-module-v2-in-ethereum-staking-overhaul)

* **[World](https://thedefiant.io/news/infrastructure/world-enters-phase-3-extends-proof-of-human-to-ai-agents)**[ extends proof-of-human to AI agents](https://thedefiant.io/news/infrastructure/world-enters-phase-3-extends-proof-of-human-to-ai-agents)

* **[Coinbase](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/coinbase-opens-launches-tab-for-new-base-solana-tokens)**[ opens a Launches tab for new tokens](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/coinbase-opens-launches-tab-for-new-base-solana-tokens)

* **[Lynq](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/lynq-partners-with-nonco-to-enable-24-7-stablecoin-liquidity-for-institutions)**[ taps Nonco for 24/7 institutional stablecoin liquidity](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/lynq-partners-with-nonco-to-enable-24-7-stablecoin-liquidity-for-institutions)_[ [Partner]](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/lynq-partners-with-nonco-to-enable-24-7-stablecoin-liquidity-for-institutions)_

Spot ether ETFs pulled in $104 million last week, roughly triple what bitcoin funds managed.

The split traces to BlackRock: its [ether fund ETHA](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/ether-etfs-pull-104m-tripling-bitcoin-s-weekly-inflows) absorbed $96.3 million over five sessions while IBIT, the largest crypto ETF, bled $95.5 million, including back-to-back withdrawals north of $200 million on Thursday and Friday. It's the second straight week ether products out-raised bitcoin's, and bitcoin's weekly haul has now dropped 55% week-over-week even as ether's held flat.

The rotation is happening while prices mark time. ETH trades around $1,940, still 61% below its 2025 high, and bitcoin sits near $64,800. Corporate treasuries lean the same way — BitMine Immersion added 104,512 ETH in 30 days and now holds 5.78 million, about 4.8% of supply. Whether allocators keep picking ether once bitcoin's outflows steady is what the next few weekly prints decide.
